# Restoration models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

9 restoration models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: the restored (upscaled) image, `model.scale` x the input size, RGB in [0, 1]. `tile=` runs large images in overlapping tiles (as ComfyUI).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 512x512: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## Real-ESRGAN

Real-ESRGAN (Wang et al., Tencent ARC, 2021): upscales real-world photos (x4, x2) and anime images (x4) with an RRDB network trained on synthetic degradations (blur, noise, JPEG); the classic ComfyUI upscaler. BSD-3-Clause code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `realesrgan-x4plus` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 631<br>632<br>402<br>354<br>273 | 2266 / 2496<br>2245 / 2474<br>1220 / 1434<br>1091 / 1394<br>1546 / 1594 |
| `realesrgan-x2plus` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 128<br>128<br>80.0<br>85.2<br>59.7 | 592 / 656<br>589 / 654<br>333 / 394<br>323 / 394<br>476 / 500 |
| `realesrgan-x4plus-anime-6b` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 205<br>206<br>132<br>114<br>83.1 | 2243 / 2472<br>2221 / 2450<br>1197 / 1410<br>1068 / 1370<br>1505 / 1552 |

### Measured

DIV2K validation HR images and the official bicubic LR images (x4 or x2, the model's scale), one pass without tiles; PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) on the Y channel (BT.601) of the output rounded to uint8, `scale` px border cropped, averaged over the images. Real-ESRGAN is trained for real-world degradations, not bicubic, so its PSNR is low: the numbers compare our modes with the original, not with PSNR-oriented upscalers. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

## SPAN

SPAN (Wan et al., NTIRE 2024 efficient SR winner): a small, fast x4 / x2 upscaler for clean (bicubic) images, convolutions with parameter-free attention. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `span-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 26.9<br>24.2<br>14.6<br>13.2<br>8.28 | 611 / 648<br>607 / 662<br>487 / 522<br>204 / 222<br>319 / 346 |
| `span-x2` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 24.6<br>23.5<br>14.9<br>13.2<br>7.98 | 611 / 648<br>607 / 662<br>487 / 522<br>204 / 222<br>243 / 266 |

## SwinIR

SwinIR (Liang et al., ICCVW 2021): a Swin Transformer upscaler: x4 / x2 for clean (bicubic) images and x4 for real-world photos (medium and large). Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.
